newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire mobilises for spreading war, invites allies.
newsitem.headline: Zaire mobilises for spreading war, invites allies.

text.p: Zaire has ordered a national mobilisation and called on allies to help its beleaguered mercenary-backed army combat rebels who have taken their armed campaign to the vital mining province of Shaba.
Conflict in the Heart of Africa took on wider international ramifications after Defence Ministry officials said troops from Togo, Chad and Morocco were standing by to fly to Zaire.
The Central African nation had also invited Israel and China to help train new brigades of up to 26,000 fighters, including child soldiers encouraged officially by Zaire to take up arms.

"Togo, Morocco and Chad are all prepared to send troops along with materials. Egypt has offered materials mostly to equip the infantry," a senior Defence Ministry official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"The planes for this operation have already been chartered," the official said. He could not give a definite date for the arrival of the foreign troops.
Tutsi-led rebels battling the Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba Province.

If the fall of the lake-side Shaba town of Kalemie is confirmed, the border strip under rebel control would have stretched for over 1,000 km (600 miles). The copper and cobalt mining hub around Lubumbashi is still another 800 km away.
A Zairean opposition party denounced plans for foreign intervention and called for negotiations instead.

"The Union for Democracy and Social Progress calls on the French government to reject plans for foreign intervention in Zaire, as called for by Kamanda Wa Kamanda, foreign minister for the mafia-politico-military power in Kinshasa," the opposition UDPS said in a statement issued by its representative in Paris.

"The UDPS prefers a peaceful solution of the conflict in eastern Zaire and urges above all a national unity government under the leadership of (main radical opposition leader) Etienne Tshisekedi," the party said.

Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting alongside the ethnic Tutsis who launched an armed rebellion after local authorities threatened to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda. Rebel leaders now say their objective is to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko who has ruled Zaire since 1965.
Mobutu, who has been convalescing in France from cancer, flew to Morocco for a three-day visit and talks with long-time ally King Hassan expected to centre on the fighting.

Moroccan troops helped put down a 1977 secessionist uprising in Shaba after Zairean forces were overwhelmed. They also relieved French and Belgian paratroops backing Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
The defence official said Zaire had started a nation-wide recruitment campaign for the army to train up 13 rapid intervention commando brigades of 2,000 men each.
He said China and Israel would help train the commandos at bases in the Zaire provinces of Shaba, Upper Zaire and Equateur.
Underlining Zaire's growing desperation in the face of rebel advances, the government called on youths from the age of 15 to join the special intervention brigades.
Aid officials have said renewed fighting could lead to another refugee calamity in Zaire following last year's exodus of more than half a million Hutus from camps in eastern Zaire.
They said another half million Hutus who fled fighting around camps last year and went deeper inside Zaire were now trapped in dense jungle because of the latest violence.
